title: canVoid inverts the admin check: every non-admin may void, an admin listed first may not
evidence: Array.prototype.indexOf returns -1 when the role is absent (truthy) and 0 when it is first (falsy). Traced against app.js:2 and app.js:32.
failing_case: The signed-in user in app.js:2 is roles ["viewer","billing"]. indexOf("admin") is -1, which is truthy, so canVoid returns true and the Void click at app.js:32 POSTs /api/invoices/void. A user with roles ["admin"] gets indexOf 0, canVoid returns false and the real admin is blocked. The role check is also only in the browser, so the server must enforce it too (not visible in the payload).
remediation: Use user.roles.includes("admin") (or indexOf(...) !== -1), add a test with roles [], ["viewer"], ["admin"], ["viewer","admin"], and enforce the role on the server.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send has no network-failure handling and shows nothing on success
evidence: The fetch is not in a try/catch, so an offline or DNS failure rejects the async handler (unhandled rejection, no UI). On success app.js:28 only increments sentCount, which nothing reads, and nothing is shown or cleared.
failing_case: Go offline and click Send invoice: the promise rejects, the console logs an unhandled rejection, and the user sees no message, so they cannot tell if the invoice went. With a working network, a click shows no confirmation and the lines stay, so the user clicks again (see the tooSoon finding) and sends a duplicate.
remediation: Wrap the call in try/catch, show an inline status region for sending, sent (with what was sent) and failed (cause plus Retry), disable the button while pending, and clear or lock the lines after confirmed success.

title: validQuantity accepts empty, blank, negative, zero, fractional and Infinity quantities
evidence: isNaN("") and isNaN(" ") are false because they coerce to 0; isNaN("-5"), isNaN("0"), isNaN("1.5"), isNaN("Infinity") are all false. app.js:19 relies on it, and index.html:16 only hints numeric via inputmode.
failing_case: Leave Quantity empty and press Add line with price 10: validQuantity("") is true, Number("") is 0, so a line with qty 0 is pushed and the list shows 0 × 10.00. Quantity -5 adds a line that lowers the total, and Infinity makes the total Infinity. These lines are then POSTed by the Send button.
remediation: Parse once with a validator: /^[1-9]\d*$/ (or Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 and a sane upper bound) and have it return the parsed number. Require qty in the HTML as well.

title: tooSoon never trips because lastSend is never assigned; double send of an invoice is not prevented
evidence: grep of lastSend: declared guards.js:22 as 0 and only read at guards.js:24; app.js:24-29 never sets it. Date.now() minus 0 is about 1.7e12, so the comparison is always false. The handler also does not disable the button while the fetch is pending.
failing_case: Double-click Send invoice (or click again while the POST at app.js:26 is pending). Both clicks pass tooSoon(), two POSTs of the same lines go out, and the customer is invoiced twice.
remediation: Disable the button (or hold an in-flight flag) from click until the response, and send an idempotency key so the server drops a repeat. If the time guard stays, set lastSend = Date.now() when a send starts.

title: escapeHtml leaves double quotes unescaped and its output goes into a title="..." attribute
evidence: guards.js:5 replaces only &, < and >. app.js:8 places the result inside a double-quoted attribute and then assigns it with innerHTML. The client field is free text (index.html:14).
failing_case: Type client name: x" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)" style="position:fixed;inset:0 and add the line. The rendered markup is <a href="#" title="x" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)" ...>, a full-viewport element that runs script on hover. A <script>-free payload passes the escaper because no < or > is needed.
remediation: Build the list with createElement and textContent/setAttribute, or make escapeHtml also encode " and ' (" ') and keep one encoder per sink.
fix: not offerable: unbalanced brackets or quotes

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Invoice total is computed in render code in floating point, from unrounded prices, and does not match the rows shown
evidence: Prices are accepted with any number of decimals (app.js:18, only > 0 is checked) and each row displays price.toFixed(2) at app.js:8, while the total sums the raw price. There is no single money function with a test.
failing_case: Add 3 lines of qty 1 at price 0.005: each row shows 0.01 (toFixed rounds the float, may show 0.01 or 0.00 depending on representation), and the total shows 0.01 for a displayed sum of 0.03. The same math is sent to the server as raw floats in app.js:26.
remediation: Store prices in integer minor units, round once when a line is added, put the total in one pure tested function, and have the server recompute it.

title: Invalid input is dropped silently: no message, no focus, nothing says why Add line did nothing
evidence: The handler returns with no output. index.html has no error element, no aria-invalid and no aria-describedby. Only client has required.
failing_case: Enter a price of 12,50 (comma) or 0 and press Add line: Number("12,50") is NaN, the handler returns, and the form looks unchanged. A keyboard or screen-reader user gets no feedback at all.
remediation: On failure, write an error next to the field ("Unit price must be a number above 0, for example 12.50"), set aria-invalid and move focus to that field; announce it in a role=alert region.

title: Void is destructive with no confirm, no target invoice and no success or failure-on-network feedback
evidence: index.html:24 renders the Void button next to Send with the same weight. The handler posts an empty body (no invoice id), asks no confirmation, shows nothing on success, and has no try/catch for a rejected fetch.
failing_case: Click Void invoice by mistake: the POST is sent immediately with no confirmation or undo. The server cannot know which invoice is meant from this request. On success the page does not change, so the user cannot tell it worked.
remediation: Send the invoice id, ask for confirmation naming the invoice, show a result message, catch network errors, and show the button only to users the server allows.

title: Each line's client name is a link that goes nowhere: href="#" scrolls to top and is a tab stop with no purpose
evidence: The anchor text is the client name, the target is #, and no handler is attached to it. It receives focus and has a focus ring (styles.css:5).
failing_case: Tab through the page after adding 5 lines: five extra tab stops that, when activated, jump the page to the top and add # to the URL.
remediation: Render the client as plain text (span) unless it links to a real client page.

title: The whole list is re-announced on every add because render replaces all of its markup
evidence: app.js:7 sets list.innerHTML for the whole list on every submit, and aria-live="polite" on the ul makes a screen reader read the replaced content.
failing_case: With 10 lines present, adding the 11th makes a screen reader read all 11 items again, and the changed total is not announced with it.
remediation: Append only the new li, or move the live region to a short status message ("Added: Acme 2 x 10.00. Total 20.00").
